the-awakening-of-helena-richie: Margaret Deland's 1906 novel follows Helena Richie, a young widow in a quiet New England town who falls deeply in love with an unmarried man. Their bond sets the whole community talking and forces Helena to choose between her heart and the strict rules around her. The book became one of the era's most talked-about stories of passion, guilt, and a woman's right to her own life.
the-prairie: James Fenimore Cooper closes his Leatherstocking Tales with Natty Bumppo — Hawkeye — now a very old man on the western prairies. Far from the forests of his youth, the aging scout faces Sioux warriors, a lost family, and the end of his wandering life. Poignant and grand, it is the farewell of American literature's first great frontier hero.
field-and-hedgerow-being-the-last-essays: Richard Jefferies' final essays — written as his health failed — glow with love for the English countryside. Fields, hedgerows, and wild things are seen with an almost painful beauty. Among the most moving nature writings in the language. These last essays, written as his strength failed, rank among the most beautiful nature writings in English.
the-marquis-of-lossie: George MacDonald's Scottish novel continues the story of Malcolm — now the Marquis of Lossie — among fisher folk and London society. The author's deep faith and love for Scotland shine throughout. A warm, wise sequel to a beloved tale. From herring boats to Mayfair drawing rooms, MacDonald's tale moves with grace and truth.
the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: Holmes' earlier poems from 1830 to 1836 open the collected edition — the young Bostonian's first flights in verse. Old Ironsides appears here, the famous poem that saved a frigate from the breakers. The bright dawn of a long and beloved literary career.
